Experiment – 7: Implementation of Classification Algorithms such as Logistic Regression or 
K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)
1. Aim:
Implementation of classification algorithms such as Logistic Regression and K-Nearest 
Neighbors (KNN) on the Kaggle Titanic dataset to predict passenger survival.
2. Objectives:
· Understand the concept of classification in machine learning.
· Perform basic preprocessing of a real-world Kaggle dataset.
· Handle missing values and categorical attributes before classification.
· Implement Logistic Regression and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) using Scikit-learn.
· Evaluate and compare the performance of classification models.
3. Outcomes: After study of this experiment, the student will be able to
· Explain the basic concept of classification and its applications.
· Identify and preprocess numerical, categorical and missing data.
· Implement Logistic Regression and KNN on a real-world dataset.
· Evaluate models using accuracy, confusion matrix, precision, recall and F1-score.
· Compare the performance of two classification algorithms.
4. Prerequisite:
Fundamentals of Python Programming and basic knowledge of Data Science, Pandas and 
machine learning.
5. Requirements:
Google Colab Notebook
Kaggle account and Titanic dataset (train.csv)

6. Pre-Experiment Exercise:
Brief Theory:
Classification is a supervised machine learning technique used to assign observations to 
predefined classes. In this experiment, the target variable is Survived, where 0 represents did not 
survive and 1 represents survived.
The Kaggle Titanic dataset contains passenger information such as PassengerId, Survived, Pclass, 
Name, Sex, Age, SibSp, Parch, Ticket, Fare, Cabin and Embarked. Some attributes contain 
missing values, making the dataset suitable for demonstrating preprocessing before classification.
The experiment is divided into two parts-Part A deals with Logistic Regression and Part B deals 
with K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN).
Part A: Applying Logistic Regression
Logistic Regression is a supervised classification algorithm used to estimate the probability of an 
observation belonging to a class. For the Titanic dataset, it is used to predict whether a passenger 
survived or did not survive.
Before training, categorical attributes such as Sex and Embarked are converted into numerical 
form. Missing values in Age and Embarked are handled using suitable imputation methods.
Part B: Applying K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)
K-Nearest Neighbors is a supervised classification algorithm that classifies a new observation 
based on the classes of its nearest training observations. The value of K represents the number of 
neighbors considered.
Feature scaling is important for KNN because it uses distance to identify neighboring 
observations. In this experiment, the input features are standardized before applying KNN.
Model Evaluation
Classification models can be evaluated using accuracy, confusion matrix, precision, recall and 
F1-score.
Accuracy is the proportion of correctly classified observations out of all observations. A 
confusion matrix shows the number of correct and incorrect predictions for each class.
